presentation.homeIntroduction: Explore David and Goliath, then return to 1 Samuel 17 in your Bible.
presentation.completionInvitation: Keep reading 1 Samuel 17 in your Bible.

reflection.prompt: Read 1 Samuel 17:45–47 in your Bible. What does David's trust teach you about GOD? What would you like to ask or explore as you read the chapter?

questions.question: Who did David say had delivered him before?
Why did David put off Saul's armor?
How many smooth stones did David choose?
What does David say about how the LORD saves?

story.title: David and Goliath
story.description: Explore 1 Samuel 17, remember the source, and reflect on GOD.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: 1 Samuel 17 describes a battle setting. Jesse sent David from Bethlehem with provisions for his brothers. Read the chapter in your Bible as you explore this adventure.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: David heard Goliath's challenge and spoke about the living GOD. The people around him were afraid. Read 1 Samuel 17:23–37 for the full account.

objective.title: Remember David's words
objective.instruction: Read 1 Samuel 17:37, then choose the answer supported by the passage.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Saul offered David armor. David tried it, said he had not tested it, and put it off. Then he took his staff, chose five smooth stones from the brook, and carried his sling.

objective.title: Read about the armor
objective.instruction: Why did David put off the armor?

objective.title: Read about the stones
objective.instruction: How many smooth stones does the passage say David chose?

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: David spoke about the name of the LORD and said the battle belongs to the LORD. The chapter says David prevailed with a sling and a stone, and Goliath died. This adventure does not recreate the violence.

objective.title: Read David's message
objective.instruction: Choose the explanation supported by 1 Samuel 17:47.
objective.hint: Read the verse in your Bible.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: David's words point beyond his own strength to GOD. Continue reading 1 Samuel 17 and consider what the chapter teaches about GOD.
